Thank you for installing {{ .Chart.Name }}.

Your release is named {{ .Release.Name }}.

The controller and CRDs have been installed in namespace {{ .Release.Namespace }}.

To verify the installation:

  kubectl get pods -n {{ .Release.Namespace }}
  kubectl get customresourcedefinitions

To learn more about the release, try:

  $ helm status {{ .Release.Name }} -n {{ .Release.Namespace }}
  $ helm get all {{ .Release.Name }} -n {{ .Release.Namespace }}

Approval note (Manual-mode Loops, `approval.mode: Manual`):

  `cox approve <loop>` and `cox reject <loop> --reason <reason>` read the Loop
  with `get` and set the PlanApproved / PlanRejected conditions on its
  `loops/status` subresource. Both also read PLAN.md from the workspace through
  a short-lived peek pod, so the user needs pod RBAC in the Loop's namespace as
  well. The chart installs no user-facing role by default, so unless you bind
  one, the API server rejects both commands (the operator's own role grants
  these to its ServiceAccount, not to you).
{{- if .Values.rbac.helpers.enabled }}

  This release installed the helper roles (rbac.helpers.enabled=true): bind
  the {{ include "coxswain.resourceName" (dict "suffix" "loop-editor-role" "context" $) }} role to a user or group to
  grant the Loop access `cox approve`/`reject` need (it grants reading `loops`
  and writing the `loops/status` subresource):
{{- if .Values.rbac.namespaced }}

    kubectl create rolebinding <name> --role={{ include "coxswain.resourceName" (dict "suffix" "loop-editor-role" "context" $) }} --user=<user> -n {{ .Release.Namespace }}

  That helper Role is installed in this release namespace, so the binding
  covers Loops in {{ .Release.Namespace }} only.
{{- else }}

    kubectl create rolebinding <name> --clusterrole={{ include "coxswain.resourceName" (dict "suffix" "loop-editor-role" "context" $) }} --user=<user> -n <loop-namespace>

  The helper is a ClusterRole (rbac.namespaced=false), but a RoleBinding is
  namespaced: create one in each namespace whose Loops you want to approve.
{{- end }}

  The helper role does NOT grant the peek-pod rules: bind a Role in the Loop's
  namespace granting `create`, `get` and `delete` on `pods` and `get` on
  `pods/log`.
{{- end }}

Without such a binding, `cox approve`/`reject` are rejected by the API server
(the operator still advances Auto-mode Loops — only Manual-mode approval needs
the binding).
